theory.title: Present Perfect Simple и Continuous

head: Present Perfect Simple
Present Perfect Continuous
rows: результат, количество: I've written three emails.
процесс, длительность: I've been writing emails all morning.
законченное действие: I've painted the room.
незаконченное или следы: I've been painting (у меня краска на руках).
глаголы состояния: I've known her for years.
активные действия: I've been learning Spanish for a year.

theory.tip: С know, like, have (владеть), be, believe — только Simple. How many / how much → Simple; How long → чаще Continuous.

exercises.title: Cyberchondria
exercises.text: Have you ever searched your symptoms online and convinced yourself you had a rare disease? Doctors have been seeing more and more patients with 'cyberchondria' — anxiety caused by medical internet searches. The problem is that search engines show dramatic results first: a simple headache might appear next to articles about brain tumours. Researchers have found that people who search repeatedly become more anxious, not less. Their advice: if you've been worrying about a symptom for days, call a doctor rather than opening another tab.

questions.text: Cyberchondria is anxiety caused by medical internet ___.

theory.title: Прилагательные как существительные
theory.text: the + прилагательное = группа людей (множественное число): the rich, the poor, the elderly, the young, the unemployed, the homeless. Национальности на -sh, -ch, -ese: the British, the French, the Japanese.
theory.tip: Глагол во множественном числе: The rich are getting richer. Об одном человеке — a rich man, an elderly woman.

theory.title: Порядок прилагательных
theory.text: Мнение → размер → возраст → форма → цвет → происхождение → материал → назначение + существительное.

exercises.title: Fast fashion
exercises.text: The average person now buys 60% more clothes than fifteen years ago, but keeps them for half as long. This is 'fast fashion': cheap, trendy clothes produced quickly and sold in huge quantities. The environmental cost is enormous — making a single cotton T-shirt uses about 2,700 litres of water. Some young people are fighting back by buying second-hand, renting clothes for special occasions or simply wearing the same plain, good-quality items for years.

questions.text: People buy ___% more clothes than fifteen years ago.

questions.statement: Some young people rent clothes for special occasions.
